library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: Goryanin I, Damms B, Goryanin I. A Systems Pharmacology Model of
  Aging Identifies Optimal Combination Therapies With Secondary Benefits on
  Weight Loss and Metabolic Health. *CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol*.
  2026;15:e70322.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70322> (PMCID PMC13454951)
* Model code: the authors deposit the model as an SBML Level 3 Version 2 file
  (model `IQANOVA_GLP1_Ageing_QSP`, Supporting Information S2), together with
  the digitised calibration data (S3, `all_synthetic_data.csv`), an
  identifiability report (S6) and a model-informed drug development report
  (S7) whose Eqs. 1-10 restate the SBML.

The paper builds a deterministic quantitative systems pharmacology model in
which aging is a pharmacologically modifiable endpoint. A semaglutide exposure
term drives body-weight loss, HbA1c reduction and transient nausea; two
time-averaged scenario scalars stand in for a drug combination and drive four
aging states (damage, repair capacity, frailty, biological age gap); and five
biomarkers are read out from production-degradation equations. The authors
compare GLP-1 receptor agonist + SGLT2 inhibitor + metformin (the "metabolic"
combination) with GLP-1 receptor agonist + SGLT2 inhibitor + rapamycin (the
"aging" combination).

**Read this first.** The packaged model is a verbatim translation of the
deposited SBML, and that SBML does not reproduce the paper's own results. It
falls short of the calibration fit in Figure 2. It cannot give dose-dependent
plateaus or a nausea peak. It matches one of the twelve bars of the Figure 6
bar chart. Its cystatin C and leptin states settle below -100% change. The
sections below quantify each gap. The model is packaged so that the published
equations and values can be inspected and simulated. It is not a validated
predictor of any of the paper's endpoints.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Goryanin_2026_semaglutide_aging_qsp")
```

# Population

The model represents a single typical adult with obesity and/or type 2
diabetes; there is no between-subject or residual variability and no virtual
population. The semaglutide layer was calibrated to arm-level mean
trajectories digitised from STEP 1 (2.4 mg) and STEP 2 (1.0 and 2.4 mg) at
weeks 0, 4, 12, 24, 36/40, 52 and 68. The aging and biomarker layers were
anchored to literature-derived population targets rather than to individual
data (Methods, "Staged Calibration Strategy and Provenance"). The same
information is available as `readModelDb("Goryanin_2026_semaglutide_aging_qsp")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `expo = D / (1 + D / ed50)` | n/a | SBML assignment rule `E_sema`; S7 Eq. 1 (the main text prints `D / (EC50 + D)`; see Assumptions) |
| `d/dt(bwloss) = kbwloss * expo * (1 - bwloss / emax_bwloss)` | n/a | SBML R01; S7 Eq. 2; Methods "Metabolic and Pharmacodynamic Layer" |
| `d/dt(hba1cred) = khba1cred * expo * (1 - hba1cred / emax_hba1cred)` | n/a | SBML R02; S7 Eq. 3 |
| `d/dt(nausea) = knausea * expo * (1 - moderator1) - kout_nausea * nausea` | n/a | SBML R03; S7 Eq. 4; Methods |
| `d/dt(moderator1) = ktol * nausea * (1 - moderator1)` | n/a | SBML R04; S7 Eq. 5; Methods |
| `d/dt(damage) = kdam * (1 - drug_d) - krep_clear * repair * damage` | n/a | SBML R05; S7 Eq. 6; Layer Coupling equations |
| `d/dt(repair) = krapa * drug_r - krep_deg * repair` | n/a | SBML R06; S7 Eq. 7; Layer Coupling equations |
| `d/dt(frailty) = kfra * damage - kfra_rep * repair` | n/a | SBML R07; S7 Eq. 8; Layer Coupling equations |
| `d/dt(bioagegap) = kbag * (damage - 0.5 * repair)` | n/a | SBML R08; S7 Eq. 9 (the main text prints `k_B * DAM - 0.5 * REP`) |
| `d/dt(cysc) = kin_cysc * 1 * (-11) - kout_cysc * cysc` | n/a | SBML R09_CysC kinetic law, verbatim |
| `d/dt(leptin) = kin_leptin * 1 * (-11) - kout_leptin * leptin` | n/a | SBML R09_LEP kinetic law, verbatim |
| `nausea(0)`, `repair(0)` | 2, 0.1 | SBML species `initialAmount` |
| `ed50` | 2.0 mg | Table 2 `EC50`; SBML `EC50` |
| `kbwloss`, `emax_bwloss` | 0.20 /week, 15.0% | Table 2 `k_W`, `Emax_W`; SBML |
| `khba1cred`, `emax_hba1cred` | 0.15 /week, 1.80% points | Table 2 `k_A`, `Emax_A`; SBML |
| `knausea`, `ktol` | 0.35, 0.04 /week | Table 2 `k_N`, `k_T`; SBML |
| `kout_nausea` | 0.15 /week | Methods nausea equation; SBML R03 literal |
| `kdam`, `krep_clear`, `krep_deg`, `krapa` | 0.10, 0.80, 0.25, 0.45 | Table 2 `k_dam`, `k_rep`, `k_Rdeg`, `k_Rap`; SBML |
| `kfra`, `kfra_rep`, `kbag` | 0.30, 0.50, 0.40 /week | S6 aging-layer RSE table `k_F`, `k_Frep`, `k_B`; S7 R5 (`k_F`); SBML |
| `drug_d`, `drug_r` | 0.50, 0.60 (aging); 0.40, 0.10 (metabolic) | Methods "Layer Coupling Architecture"; SBML `drug_D_ageing`, `drug_R_ageing` |
| `kin_cysc`, `kout_cysc` | 6.8, 0.48 /week | SBML `k_CysC_prod`, `k_CysC_deg` |
| `kin_leptin`, `kout_leptin` | 14.1, 0.55 /week | SBML `k_Leptin_prod`, `k_Leptin_deg` |

Units of every ODE term, time in weeks: `expo` is in mg, as the SBML
declares no unit for it. `kbwloss * expo` is then in % per week only if
`kbwloss` is read as % per (week x mg). The paper and the SBML give it as
1/week, and the same reading applies to `khba1cred` and `knausea`. `ktol *
nausea` must be in 1/week, so `ktol` is 1/(week x % prevalence). `krep_clear *
repair * damage` is in a.u. per week with `krep_clear` in 1/(week x a.u.).
The authors state every rate constant only as wk^-1, so these unit readings
are the maintainers' dimensional bookkeeping, not values from the source.

# Simulation

The two calibration arms are semaglutide 1.0 mg and 2.4 mg once weekly for 68
weeks. The dose reaches the model as the covariate `DOSE_SEMAGLUTIDE_INJ_MG`
because the model has no PK. The combination scenarios differ only in
`drug_d` and `drug_r`, which are overridden per solve.

```{r simulate}
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 68, by = 0.5), 4, 12, 24, 36, 40, 52)))
make_arm <- function(dose_mg, arm, id) {
  data.frame(
    id = id, time = obs_times, evid = 0, cmt = "bwloss",
    DOSE_SEMAGLUTIDE_INJ_MG = dose_mg, arm = arm
  )
}
ev_cal <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_arm(1.0, "1.0 mg", 1L),
  make_arm(2.4, "2.4 mg", 2L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_cal[, c("id", "time")]))

# Tight step tolerances so the closed-form checks below test the equations,
# not LSODA's default 1e-6 relative error.
sim_cal <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = ev_cal, keep = "arm", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
) |> as.data.frame()

scenarios <- data.frame(
  combo = c("Metabolic (GLP-1 RA + SGLT2i + metformin)",
            "Aging (GLP-1 RA + SGLT2i + rapamycin)",
            "Untreated aging layer"),
  drug_d = c(0.40, 0.50, 0),
  drug_r = c(0.10, 0.60, 0)
)
sim_combo <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), function(i) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod, events = make_arm(2.4, "2.4 mg", 1L),
    params = c(drug_d = scenarios$drug_d[i], drug_r = scenarios$drug_r[i]),
    rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
  ) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(combo = scenarios$combo[i])
}))
```

# Internal consistency of the translation

These checks show that the rxode2 file integrates the SBML equations as
written. Each compares the numerical solution with the closed form of the
same equations and the same parameter values, so a tight tolerance is
correct.

```{r closed-form}
ini_val <- function(nm) {
  df <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$iniDf
  df$est[df$name == nm]
}
ed50 <- ini_val("ed50")

# Weight and HbA1c: d/dt(x) = k E (1 - x / Emax), x(0) = 0, so
# x(t) = Emax (1 - exp(-k E t / Emax)).
cf <- sim_cal |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    E = DOSE_SEMAGLUTIDE_INJ_MG / (1 + DOSE_SEMAGLUTIDE_INJ_MG / ed50),
    bw_cf = ini_val("emax_bwloss") *
      (1 - exp(-ini_val("kbwloss") * E * time / ini_val("emax_bwloss"))),
    a_cf = ini_val("emax_hba1cred") *
      (1 - exp(-ini_val("khba1cred") * E * time / ini_val("emax_hba1cred")))
  )
err_bw <- max(abs(cf$bwloss - cf$bw_cf))
err_a <- max(abs(cf$hba1cred - cf$a_cf))
# Measured ~1e-9 % points with rtol = 1e-10.
stopifnot(err_bw < 1e-6, err_a < 1e-6)

# Repair: d/dt(R) = krapa drug_r - krep_deg R, R(0) = 0.1.
# Cystatin C / leptin: d/dt(B) = -11 kin - kout B, B(0) = 0, steady state
# -11 kin / kout.
aging <- sim_combo |>
  dplyr::filter(combo == scenarios$combo[2]) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    rep_ss = ini_val("krapa") * 0.60 / ini_val("krep_deg"),
    rep_cf = rep_ss + (0.1 - rep_ss) * exp(-ini_val("krep_deg") * time),
    cysc_cf = -11 * ini_val("kin_cysc") / ini_val("kout_cysc") *
      (1 - exp(-ini_val("kout_cysc") * time)),
    leptin_cf = -11 * ini_val("kin_leptin") / ini_val("kout_leptin") *
      (1 - exp(-ini_val("kout_leptin") * time))
  )
stopifnot(
  max(abs(aging$repair - aging$rep_cf)) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(aging$cysc - aging$cysc_cf)) < 1e-5,
  max(abs(aging$leptin - aging$leptin_cf)) < 1e-5
)
```

The exposure term saturates at `ed50` = 2 mg, which the identifiability report
calls "analytically bounded in [0, 1)". With the SBML form `D / (1 + D /
EC50)`, E is 0.67 at 1.0 mg and 1.09 at 2.4 mg. It tends to 2, not 1, as the
dose grows.

# Comparison with the calibration fit (Figure 2)

The calibration data deposited in S3 (`all_synthetic_data.csv`, column
`mean`) are transcribed below. The Figure 2 model curves themselves were read
from the figure by the maintainers: a 68-week weight loss of about 10.9% and
15.2%, an HbA1c reduction of about 1.3 and 1.6 points, and a nausea peak of
about 25% and 30% near week 12, for 1.0 and 2.4 mg.

```{r figure-2, fig.height = 6}
calib <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,     ~time, ~bw,   ~hba1c, ~nausea,
  "1.0 mg",  0,     0.0,  0.0,    2,
  "1.0 mg",  4,    -2.1, -0.3,   17,
  "1.0 mg", 12,    -5.8, -0.7,   21,
  "1.0 mg", 24,    -8.2, -1.1,   16,
  "1.0 mg", 40,    -9.4, -1.3,   10,
  "1.0 mg", 52,    -9.9, -1.4,    6,
  "1.0 mg", 68,   -10.4, -1.5,    2,
  "2.4 mg",  0,     0.0,  0.0,    2,
  "2.4 mg",  4,    -3.1, -0.4,   21,
  "2.4 mg", 12,    -7.5, -0.9,   25,
  "2.4 mg", 24,   -11.0, -1.4,   19,
  "2.4 mg", 40,   -13.3, -1.6,   12,
  "2.4 mg", 52,   -14.2, -1.7,    7,
  "2.4 mg", 68,   -14.9, -1.8,    2
)

long_sim <- sim_cal |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    arm, time,
    `Body-weight change (%)` = -bwloss,
    `HbA1c change (% points)` = -hba1cred,
    `Nausea prevalence (%)` = nausea
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(arm, time), names_to = "endpoint")
long_dat <- calib |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    arm, time,
    `Body-weight change (%)` = bw,
    `HbA1c change (% points)` = hba1c,
    `Nausea prevalence (%)` = nausea
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(arm, time), names_to = "endpoint")

ggplot(long_sim, aes(time, value, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = long_dat, shape = 21, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "Week", y = NULL, colour = "Semaglutide",
    caption = paste(
      "Lines: packaged model (deposited SBML). Points: calibration data (S3).",
      "Compare Figure 2 of Goryanin 2026."
    )
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r figure-2-table}
at68 <- sim_cal |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 68) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, bwloss, hba1cred, nausea)
peak <- sim_cal |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(nausea_peak = max(nausea), .groups = "drop")
cmp2 <- at68 |>
  dplyr::left_join(peak, by = "arm") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    calib |>
      dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        bw_data = -bw[time == 68], a_data = -hba1c[time == 68],
        nausea_peak_data = max(nausea), .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "arm"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(bw_fig2 = c(10.9, 15.2), a_fig2 = c(1.3, 1.6),
                nausea_fig2 = c(25, 30))

cmp2 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    arm,
    "Weight loss 68 wk, model (%)" = round(bwloss, 2),
    "Weight loss 68 wk, S3 data (%)" = bw_data,
    "Weight loss 68 wk, Figure 2 curve (%)" = bw_fig2,
    "HbA1c reduction 68 wk, model" = round(hba1cred, 2),
    "HbA1c reduction 68 wk, S3 data" = a_data,
    "HbA1c reduction 68 wk, Figure 2 curve" = a_fig2,
    "Nausea peak, model (%)" = round(nausea_peak, 2),
    "Nausea peak, S3 data (%)" = nausea_peak_data,
    "Nausea peak, Figure 2 curve (%)" = nausea_fig2
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(Arm = arm) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Deposited model against the paper's calibration targets.")

# Pin the documented non-reproduction. The model is deterministic, so these
# values are fixed by the equations; if a future edit moves them, either the
# translation changed or the source was corrected.
stopifnot(
  abs(cmp2$bwloss - c(6.80, 9.42)) < 0.01,
  abs(cmp2$hba1cred - c(1.76, 1.80)) < 0.01,
  # Nausea never rises above its 2% starting value by more than 0.1 point.
  cmp2$nausea_peak < 2.1,
  # Gap to the calibration data: more than 3 points of weight loss short.
  cmp2$bw_data - cmp2$bwloss > 3
)
```

The packaged model reaches about two thirds of the calibrated 68-week weight
loss. The HbA1c reduction is close to `emax_hba1cred` = 1.8 in both arms. It
comes out slightly above the data at 1.0 mg and at the data at 2.4 mg. Nausea
never shows the peak at all: it falls monotonically from its 2% start. Two
features of Figure 2 cannot be produced by these equations at any parameter
values. First, the logistic term `(1 - x / Emax)` sends every dose to the
same plateau `Emax`, so the two arms cannot plateau at different levels as the
figure shows for weight (about 10.9 vs 15.2) and HbA1c (about 1.3 vs 1.6).
Second, the steady-state nausea input `knausea * E` is below 0.4% per week, so
no rescaling of time can produce a 25-30% peak. The S3 data and the Figure 2
points also disagree with each other. At 68 weeks HbA1c is 1.5 in S3 and about
1.3 in the figure (1.0 mg), and nausea at week 0 is 2% in S3 and 0% in the
figure.

# Comparison with the combination scenarios (Figure 6)

The bar chart of 52-week changes (Figure 6) reports, for the metabolic and
aging combinations respectively: body weight -16 / -13%, HbA1c -1.35 / -0.95
points, DAM -12 / -22, REP +8 / +22, FRA -8 / -13 and BAG -11 / -20. The
deposited model-calibration table (S7 R7.1) gives the aging-layer states in
"a.u. x 100". The table below therefore shows the model's 52-week change from
baseline multiplied by 100.

```{r figure-6}
fig6 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~combo, ~state, ~published,
  scenarios$combo[1], "bwloss", -16,
  scenarios$combo[2], "bwloss", -13,
  scenarios$combo[1], "hba1cred", -1.35,
  scenarios$combo[2], "hba1cred", -0.95,
  scenarios$combo[1], "damage", -12,
  scenarios$combo[2], "damage", -22,
  scenarios$combo[1], "repair", 8,
  scenarios$combo[2], "repair", 22,
  scenarios$combo[1], "frailty", -8,
  scenarios$combo[2], "frailty", -13,
  scenarios$combo[1], "bioagegap", -11,
  scenarios$combo[2], "bioagegap", -20
)
wk52 <- sim_combo |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0, 52)) |>
  dplyr::select(combo, time, bwloss, hba1cred, damage, repair, frailty, bioagegap) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(combo, time), names_to = "state") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = value, names_prefix = "t") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    model = dplyr::case_when(
      state == "bwloss" ~ -t52,
      state == "hba1cred" ~ -t52,
      TRUE ~ 100 * (t52 - t0)
    )
  )
cmp6 <- fig6 |>
  dplyr::left_join(wk52 |> dplyr::select(combo, state, model), by = c("combo", "state"))

cmp6 |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = signif(model, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Combination = combo, State = state,
    "Figure 6 bar" = published, "Model, 52-week change" = model
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "52-week changes. Weight and HbA1c in % and % points (sign as in",
    "Figure 6); aging states as change from baseline x 100 (a.u.)."
  ))

rep_met <- cmp6$model[cmp6$state == "repair" & cmp6$combo == scenarios$combo[1]]
rep_age <- cmp6$model[cmp6$state == "repair" & cmp6$combo == scenarios$combo[2]]
stopifnot(
  # The one bar that reproduces: metabolic-combination REP +8.
  abs(rep_met - 8) < 0.5,
  # Aging-combination REP is about four times the +22 bar.
  rep_age > 90,
  # Weight loss does not depend on drug_d / drug_r in the deposited model.
  abs(diff(cmp6$model[cmp6$state == "bwloss"])) < 1e-6
)
```

Only the metabolic-combination REP bar is reproduced. In the deposited
equations, body weight and HbA1c depend on the semaglutide dose alone, so the
two combinations cannot differ on them. The model gives about 8% weight loss
at 2.4 mg in both, against -16 and -13 in the figure. `damage` starts at zero,
so it can only rise from baseline. `frailty` and `bioagegap` have no
first-order loss, so they drift linearly for as long as the damage-repair
balance is non-zero. In the aging combination, frailty falls by about 25 a.u.
over 52 weeks.

```{r aging-trajectories}
sim_combo |>
  dplyr::select(time, combo, damage, repair, frailty, bioagegap) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(time, combo), names_to = "state") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = combo)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~state, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "State (a.u.)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Aging-layer states of the deposited model under the three scenarios.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

# Biomarker layer (Figure 5)

The paper writes the biomarkers as `dB_i/dt = k_prod_i * pot_drug * sigma_i *
(1 + gamma_i * DAM) - k_deg_i * B_i`; S7 Eq. 10 drops the `gamma_i` term.
Neither `sigma_i` nor `gamma_i` is reported, and neither is the rule that
combines `pot_drug` across a three-drug combination. In the SBML, the GDF15,
adiponectin and eGDR reactions have empty kinetic laws, so they are not
packaged. The cystatin C and leptin reactions read `k_prod * pot_semaglutide *
(-11) - k_deg * B`. They are packaged verbatim, and they settle at changes
that no serum concentration can reach.

```{r biomarkers}
bm <- sim_cal |>
  dplyr::filter(arm == "2.4 mg", time == 52) |>
  dplyr::select(cysc, leptin)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Biomarker = c("Cystatin C", "Leptin"),
    "Model 52-week change (%)" = round(c(bm$cysc, bm$leptin), 1),
    "S3 semaglutide arm, 52 weeks (%)" = c(-7, -15),
    "Figure 5, 52 weeks (normalised, metabolic / aging)" = c("0.91 / 0.84", "0.66 / 0.72"),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  caption = "Biomarker states of the deposited model against the published trajectories."
)
stopifnot(bm$cysc < -100, bm$leptin < -100)
```

These two states should not be used for prediction. They are included so the
deposited model is complete as published.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Source of truth.** The model follows the deposited SBML (S2). Its parameter
  values equal Table 2 of the paper and the S6 / S7 tables. Three rate
  constants, `kfra` (k_F), `kfra_rep` (k_Frep) and `kbag` (k_B), are not in
  the main text; they come from the S6 identifiability table and the SBML.
  The biomarker constants come from the SBML only.
- **Exposure function.** The main text prints `E = D / (EC50 + D)`, while
  the SBML assignment rule and S7 Eq. 1 use `D / (1 + D / EC50)`. The two
  differ by a factor of EC50. The code's form is used; the printed form gives
  even less weight loss (3.9% and 5.9% at 68 weeks).
- **Biological age gap.** The main text prints `k_B * DAM - 0.5 * REP`. The
  SBML and S7 Eq. 9 use `k_B * (DAM - 0.5 * REP)`, and the code's form is used.
- **Scenario scalars.** The SBML wires `drug_D_ageing` = 0.50 and
  `drug_R_ageing` = 0.60 into the damage and repair reactions, so these are
  the defaults of `drug_d` and `drug_r`. The metabolic combination (0.40 /
  0.10, Methods) is simulated by overriding them. Both are `fixed()`, since
  they are scenario inputs, not estimates. `ed50` is also `fixed()`: Table 2
  says it was held at a literature value in the scenario simulations. The
  nausea loss rate 0.15 /week is a literal constant in the equations, so it
  is `fixed()` too. The remaining constants are the authors' calibrated
  values and are left unfixed.
- **Non-reproduction.** The deposited model does not reproduce Figure 2, the
  S3 calibration data or eleven of the twelve Figure 6 bars, and the
  quantified gaps are pinned above. The maintainers found no reading of the
  equations, units or scenario scalars that closes them. That includes
  rescaling the nausea rate constants by 10 or 100 and normalising against an
  untreated reference. The parameter-table spreadsheet and the equations
  document that S7 (section R13) lists as part of the submission package are
  not among the published supporting files. No correction notice for the
  article was found as of 2026-11-22.
- **Biomarkers.** GDF15, adiponectin and eGDR are omitted because their SBML
  kinetic laws are empty. Their SBML constants are listed here for
  completeness: GDF15 production 10.2 and degradation 0.52 /week, adiponectin
  28.3 and 0.60, eGDR 48.5 and 0.58. The SBML drug potencies are semaglutide
  1, metformin 0.5, SGLT2 inhibitor 0.8 and rapamycin 0.6. Only the
  semaglutide potency enters a non-empty kinetic law, and it is written into
  the cystatin C and leptin equations as the factor 1.
- **Dose.** Semaglutide is a constant maintenance dose with no titration and
  no PK. It enters as `DOSE_SEMAGLUTIDE_INJ_MG`, and the SBML default is
  2.4 mg.
- **Variability.** The paper reports no between-subject or residual
  variability; none is added.
